title: httpd Module
content_markdown: This module provides an HTTP transport layer for OpenSIPS.
overview: This module provides an HTTP transport layer for OpenSIPS.
how_it_works:
Implementation of httpd module's http server is based on libmicrohttpd library.

TLS for the http server is enabled by setting the `tls_cert_file` and `tls_key_file` parameters. If this is enabled, support for plain http is disabled.

dependencies_required.name: libmicrohttpd
dependencies_required.reason: The following libraries or applications must be installed before running OpenSIPS with this module loaded: libmicrohttpd, with EPOLL support. This typically means a version newer than 0.9.50. WARNING! Please be aware about an EPOLL support regression in the libmicrohttpd library and packaging which affects the OpenSIPS httpd module, which was fixed according to the below timeline. The effect of the regression is that the HTTP reply body is sometimes never written by the library, causing the client (e.g. opensips-cli) to hang indefinitely waiting for it: versions 0.9.51 - 0.9.52 have been tested and work correctly; regression introduced in 0.9.53 (Apr 2017), lasting until 0.9.71 (May 2020); regression is fixed since 0.9.72 (Dec 2020).

exported_parameters.name: ip
exported_parameters.description: The IP address used by the HTTP server to listen for incoming requests.

exported_parameters.name: port
exported_parameters.description: The port number used by the HTTP server to listen for incoming requests.

exported_parameters.name: conn_timeout
exported_parameters.description: Auto-close TCP connections which are idle for more than the designated timeout, in seconds. Set to zero to never close any connections.
exported_parameters.notes: Note: the connection auto-close routine only seems to be executed in an "on-demand" fashion, during an HTTPD network event (e.g. on a new connection), which although not ideal, it should be good enough in practical terms.

exported_parameters.name: buf_size
exported_parameters.description: It specifies the maximum length (in bytes) of the buffer used to write in the html response. If the size of the buffer is set to zero, it will be automatically set to a quarter of the size of the pkg memory.

exported_parameters.name: post_buf_size
exported_parameters.description: It specifies the length (in bytes) of the POST HTTP requests processing buffer. For large POST request, the default value might require to be increased.

exported_parameters.name: tls_cert_file
exported_parameters.description: Public certificate file for httpd. It will be used as server-side certificate for incoming TLS connections.

exported_parameters.name: tls_key_file
exported_parameters.description: Private key of the above certificate. I must be kept in a safe place with tight permissions!

exported_parameters.name: tls_ciphers
exported_parameters.description: You can specify the list of algorithms for authentication and encryption that you allow. To obtain a list of ciphers and then choose, use the gnutls-cli application: * gnutls-cli -l
exported_parameters.notes: Do not use the NULL algorithms (no encryption) ... never!!!

exported_mi_functions.name: httpd_list_root_path
exported_mi_functions.description: Lists all the registered http root paths into the httpd module. When a request comes in, if the root parth is in the list, the request will be sent to the module that register it.

configuration_examples.title: Set `ip` parameter
configuration_examples.description:
The IP address used by the HTTP server to listen for incoming requests.

The default value is "*" (bind to all IPv6 and IPv4 interfaces).

configuration_examples.title: Set `port` parameter
configuration_examples.description:
The port number used by the HTTP server to listen for incoming requests.

The default value is 8888. Ports lower than 1024 are not accepted.

configuration_examples.title: Set `conn_timeout` parameter
configuration_examples.description:
Auto-close TCP connections which are idle for more than the designated timeout, in seconds. Set to zero to never close any connections.

Note: the connection auto-close routine only seems to be executed in an "on-demand" fashion, during an HTTPD network event (e.g. on a new connection), which although not ideal, it should be good enough in practical terms.

The default timeout is 30 seconds.

configuration_examples.title: Set `buf_size` parameter
configuration_examples.description:
It specifies the maximum length (in bytes) of the buffer used to write in the html response.

If the size of the buffer is set to zero, it will be automatically set to a quarter of the size of the pkg memory.

The default value is 0.

configuration_examples.title: Set `post_buf_size` parameter
configuration_examples.description:
It specifies the length (in bytes) of the POST HTTP requests processing buffer. For large POST request, the default value might require to be increased.

The default value is 1024. The minumal value is 256.

configuration_examples.title: Set `tls_cert_file` parameter
configuration_examples.description:
Public certificate file for httpd. It will be used as server-side certificate for incoming TLS connections.

The default value is ""

configuration_examples.title: Set `tls_key_file` parameter
configuration_examples.description:
Private key of the above certificate. I must be kept in a safe place with tight permissions!

The default value is ""

configuration_examples.title: Set `tls_key_file` parameter
configuration_examples.description:
You can specify the list of algorithms for authentication and encryption that you allow. To obtain a list of ciphers and then choose, use the gnutls-cli application:

*   gnutls-cli -l

Do not use the NULL algorithms (no encryption) ... never!!!

The default value is "SECURE256:+SECURE192:-VERS-ALL:+VERS-TLS1.2"
